speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; tell me, how long has your newborn been having trouble breathing, and what specific signs like grunting, flaring nostrils, or retractions are you noticing?

REQUEST TEST: Oxygen_Saturation

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: 88% on room air, improving with oxygen

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis in a newborn is highly suggestive of Respiratory Distress Syndrome, but I need to confirm the oxygen saturation levels and rule out other causes.

REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

What is the baby's gestational age, and were there any complications during delivery or a history of maternal diabetes?

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS: Gestational age: Born after the 32nd week. Delivery complications: Cesarean delivery. Maternal history: Gestational diabetes.
RESULTS: Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.30, PaCO2 50 mm Hg, PaO2 60 mm Hg, HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess -5.
RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) due to prematurity (born <32 weeks) with a history of maternal diabetes and cesarean delivery.
